text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Thursday private hospitals should train their own doctors to prevent a drain of skilled staff from the public sector.
-- River pollution in Malaysia has worstened, prompting the government to step up enforcement.
-- Car distributor Edaran Otomobil Nasional (EON) expects to sell its millionth car by the end of the year. It has already sold 910,000 cars since it began operations in 1985.
-- New private hospitals will only be allowed to be set up if they have a wing to cater to low-income groups, said Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim on Thursday.
-- A six-month-old girl became the 24th victim of a deadly strain of the Coxsackie B virus in the eastern Malaysian state of Sarawak.

-- Pengkalen Holdings group appears to be well on the road to recovery after reporting a pre-tax profit of 35.6 million ringgit for the year to March 31, 1997, after posting a 44.3 million ringgit loss the previous year.
-- Britain's Lloyds Bank Plc has obtained an offshore banking licence for a branch in Malaysia's international offshore financial centre of Labuan, off Borneo.
